name: Red Red
summary: Black-eyed peas stewed in a palm oil and tomato sauce, served with sweet fried plantain.
story: Red red is a Ghanaian bean stew named for the red colour of the palm oil and the ripe fried plantain. It is a staple everyday dish, filling and inexpensive, and is often served with gari.

steps.title: Cook the beans
steps.text: Cover the soaked beans with plenty of fresh water and simmer for 40 minutes until just tender but not splitting. Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking water.

steps.title: Heat the palm oil
steps.text: Warm the palm oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 2 minutes until it smells nutty and thins out. Do not let it smoke.

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: Add onion, ginger and garlic and fry for 5 minutes until the onion is soft and golden.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add tomato paste, blended tomatoes and scotch bonnet. Fry for 10-12 minutes until the sauce reduces, darkens and the oil rises to the top.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the beans, ground shrimp and a splash of the reserved water. Season with salt, cover and simmer for 10-15 minutes so the beans take on the sauce and the stew is thick.

steps.title: Fry the plantain
steps.text: Heat oil to medium-high and fry the plantain slices for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden with caramelised edges. Drain on paper towels.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the beans onto plates and serve with the plantain and gari sprinkled over.

tips: Do not add salt to the beans while boiling or they stay hard.
Red palm oil gives the signature flavour, so do not replace it if you can help it.
Mash a few beans into the sauce for a thicker, creamier stew.
Use very ripe plantain for sweetness against the spicy sauce.

swaps.swap: Use sustainably sourced unrefined palm oil if possible; otherwise vegetable oil plus a teaspoon of paprika for colour, though the flavour is milder.
Leave out for a fully vegan dish; add a pinch of smoked paprika for depth.
